compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Replaying a candidate change tells you *what would change*, not whether it is *better*. The store already carries outcome signals needing no LLM/human labeling: revise→re-review pairs, verdict flips on byte-identical material (the reviewer-noise floor), bug closes with `close_class=plan_defect`, `caused_by` links, PASS-then-completion-FAIL tickets, reopens.

`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/corpus.py` (celestine-treasonous-ewe, closed): `build_corpus(store_roots, *, cache_dir) -> manifest` recovers `plan_review_result_v1/v2` sidecars, verifies material, and writes `cache_dir / f"{manifest['content_hash']}.jsonl"` — one JSON line per VERIFIED row ONLY (`_write_cache` skips `verified=False`), fields `store, ticket_id, review_event_ts, review_event_uuid, schema, verdict, ticket_type, description, file_impact, file_impact_scope, no_file_impact_reason, children, material_fingerprint, verified, generation, reconstructed, ran_model`. The manifest itself carries only aggregate stats, no per-ticket rows.

`corpus._enumerate_event_blobs(tracker_path)` applies NO content-type filter — it returns EVERY event blob (all TYPEs), deduped by `(ticket_id, uuid)`. The `_CONTENT_TYPES = {CREATE, EDIT, FILE_IMPACT, REVIEW_RESULT}` restriction is applied one layer up, in `corpus._load_ticket_events`. So `_enumerate_event_blobs` itself already returns STATUS/COMMENT/COMPLETION_VERDICT blobs — a caller wanting those kinds just filters `_enumerate_event_blobs`'s own output by `kind`.

`config.tracker_dir_override()` reads `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`, winning verbatim over any config. A `caused_by` link is an OUTBOUND edge on the SOURCE (a bug) pointing at its TARGET (culprit); it appears inbound only on the culprit (`include_inbound=True`).

`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/mine_outcome_corpus.py` (NOT on the package import path — a docs-tree script, never imported by `src/`) defines `reopen_count`/`force_close`/`completion_verifier_fail_count` as pure functions over a per-ticket event dict.

## Approach

Build `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/labels.py`:

- **Corpus identity + ticket population**: call `corpus.build_corpus(store_roots, cache_dir=...)`; `manifest["content_hash"]` is the hash labels key to. Read `cache_dir / f"{content_hash}.jsonl"` (the SAME cache file, already VERIFIED-only) to get the corpus's ticket population, `(store, ticket_id)` pairs, per-row `review_event_ts`/`review_event_uuid`/`verdict` — this is the single driver for every downstream label; unverified rows never enter labels at all. `labels.py` refuses (raises, naming both hashes) if a caller-supplied `labels-<hash>.jsonl` disagrees with a freshly recomputed `content_hash`.
- **Finding-level source (verified-only)**: for each cache row's `review_event_uuid`, re-read that SAME `REVIEW_RESULT` blob's raw `data` via `corpus._enumerate_event_blobs` + `corpus._batch_cat` (matching the recovered blob by uuid) — never a fresh, unscoped walk of all reviews. Filter `findings` to `sidecar.surfaced_findings(data)` before any `norm_id` join (bug old-frilly-plankton).
- **Ticket-level event source (multi-store, via env override)**: for each `store_name, tracker_git_root` in `store_roots`, temporarily set `os.environ["REBAR_TRACKER_DIR"] = tracker_git_root` (restored in `finally`) around `show_ticket(ticket_id, include_inbound=True)` for that store's cache-listed ticket ids. `reopen_count`/`force_close`/`completion_verifier_fail_count` are REIMPLEMENTED directly in `labels.py` (small pure functions over a per-ticket event dict, mirroring `mine_outcome_corpus.py`'s definitions exactly), fed by calling `corpus._enumerate_event_blobs` directly and filtering its own output to `kind in {"STATUS", "COMMENT", "COMPLETION_VERDICT"}` before `corpus._batch_cat`.
- **Ticket-level labels**: `escaped_defect(X)` = UNION of (a) `X.close_class == "plan_defect"` from X's own state, (b) `X.inbound_deps` contains `relation == "caused_by"`. `completion_failed_after_pass(X)`: true when X has a cache row with `verdict == "PASS"` at `review_event_ts` T AND a recovered `COMPLETION_VERDICT` event for X with `data.verdict == "FAIL"` and `ts > T` (explicit ORDERING, not a bare count). `reopened` (`reopen_count > 0`); `escape_signals(X) = escaped_defect(X) OR completion_failed_after_pass(X) OR reopened(X) OR force_close(X)`; `clean_close` = closed AND NOT `escape_signals(X)` AND closed ≥`CLEAN_CLOSE_MIN_DAYS` days (constant, default 7) before `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` at run time (accepted imprecision, unlike the hash-pinned labels above). Each label carries its source event id(s).
- **Finding-level labels (explicit classification rule)**: for a ticket's cache rows ordered by `review_event_ts`, take each CONSECUTIVE pair (review k, review k+1) where `material_fingerprint` differs (material changed between them). For every surfaced finding `f` present in review k (keyed by `norm_id`): if `f.norm_id` is ALSO present among review k+1's surfaced findings → label that occurrence `persisted` (the author's revision did not remove it); if `f.norm_id` is ABSENT from review k+1's surfaced findings → label it `resolved_by_author` (the revision removed it). A `norm_id` first appearing in k+1 (not in k) gets neither label — it is new, not a survival outcome. `noise_flip` is separate: computed only over IDENTICAL-material consecutive pairs (`material_fingerprint` equal), comparing `verdict`, not `norm_id` sets.
- **Noise floor**: over identical-material pairs: (a) verdict flip rate; (b) per-criterion churn (Jaccard by `norm_id`); (c) per-question Pass-2 agreement — `verification` is `{"binary": {...}, "severity_attributes": {...}}`; flatten as `"binary.<key>"`/`"severity_attributes.<key>"`; for each `norm_id` in both reviews with `verification` in both, compare flattened keys present in both; agreement = `(matches)/(total compared)`, pooled across every finding/pair, published with its comparison count.
- Output `labels-<content_hash>.jsonl` plus a Markdown report with per-label-source counts, joined to `content_hash`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/labels.py` (new)
- `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/labels-report-<date>.md` (new)
- `tests/unit/evals/test_plan_replay_labels.py` (new)

## Testing

Unit: synthetic corpus of five tickets exercising each label — a bug satisfying `escaped_defect` via `close_class`, a separate origin via `inbound_deps`; `completion_failed_after_pass` true only when the FAIL event's ts is after the PASS review's `review_event_ts`; `clean_close` false when ANY of the four escape signals fires; a finding present in k, absent in k+1 (changed material) → `resolved_by_author`; a finding present in both k and k+1 (changed material) → `persisted`; a finding new in k+1 → neither label; identical-material verdict flip counted via `noise_flip`, never via the resolved/persisted path; a permanently-dropped finding excluded from the join; per-question agreement over a nested `verification` dict (one match, one mismatch, expect 0.5); an UNVERIFIED corpus row never reaches any label. Empty corpus → empty report. A stale-hash `labels-<hash>.jsonl` is refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every review and finding in the (verified) corpus carries the labels above, with source event ids; checked by the labels report counts matching independent `jq` counts over the store for `plan_defect`, `caused_by` and reopen events.
- [ ] The noise floor (verdict flip rate, per-criterion churn, per-question agreement with its pooled comparison count) is published with the identical-material pair count it was computed from; checked in the report.
- [ ] Labels are keyed to `corpus.build_corpus(...)["content_hash"]` and the loader raises when a fresh recompute disagrees with a supplied file's hash; checked by a unit test.
- [ ] No LLM calls; checked by running with no provider credentials.
compiled_state.title: Derive outcome labels and the reviewer-noise floor from the corpus (zero LLM)
